title: Enumerating candidate rules and keeping the consistent ones
summary: A small family of candidate rules is enumerated once; each new example removes the candidates it contradicts, and the readout applies the first candidate that remains.
core_idea: Enumerate a few candidate rules and drop the ones an example contradicts.

state.name: ashgrove
state.meaning: Set of candidate rules still consistent with every example so far.

update.name: step
update.latex: ashgrove_t = {h in ashgrove_(t-1) : h agrees with example x_t} (enumerate candidates)
update.plain: ashgrove_t = {h in ashgrove_(t-1) : h agrees with example x_t} (enumerate candidates)

readout.name: read
readout.latex: y_t = first candidate in ashgrove_t applied to q_t
readout.plain: y_t = first candidate in ashgrove_t applied to q_t

learning.description: Elimination of contradicted candidates; no gradient.
learning.few_shot_argument: Fixture only: no claim about learning speed is made beyond the toy case.

complexity.constants_notes: A handful of operations per symbol in the toy setting.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Fixture only: the rule is fixed by hand.

prediction.statement: One example removes every contradicted candidate.

capabilities.prediction: Finds the generating rule among eight after three examples.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: Candidate elimination is a classical idea.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: Fixture only; no difference is claimed.

toy_example.python:
import json
rules = {'add1': lambda v: v + 1, 'dbl': lambda v: 2 * v}
alive = [n for n, f in rules.items() if f(2) == 3]
print(json.dumps({'alive': alive}))
